Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.

input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "please make this into a useful textile dye log prompt for the three workshop days june 14 to june 16 at bellmere textile works, not a general guide to dyeing and not a yearly report. it should cover only the batches and equipment notes i list here. use the figures as supplied, and make the log readable for someone checking what happened on the floor. i keep forgetting to say this at the start, send the finished log to Ellis, not Leonie. dont make up a batch outcome if the notes only give an observation, and dont turn a swatch description into a signoff. a title with the date span is fine, and then arrange the material so the batch records are easy to scan. the operator names and the batch codes need to stay with the right work.

for june 14 there is batch D-214, cotton twill, 38 kg, natural indigo in vat V3, operator Mara. start time was 06:40 and the vat target was 22 C, with the recorded reading 21.5 C. the cloth was prewetted for 15 minutes. it had three dips of four minutes each and there were 12 minutes of airing between dips. rinse was at 08:12. the after-drying swatch looked deep blue. keep the measured temperature separate from the target, since they are close but not identical. this is one batch record, not a claim that every piece of cloth across the workshop came out the same. no need to describe the indigo recipe because i haven't given one.

june 15 is a different material and dye, batch M-089, 12 kg wool scarves, madder extract in kettle K2, operator Jo. the start time in the notes is 09:05. mordant was alum at 8 percent of fiber weight. the kettle was set for 80 C and readings during the run were between 78 and 81 C. hold time was 45 minutes and rinse time was 10:02. the shade note is muted rust. keep this apart from the cotton and indigo entry rather than blending the two into one process. i want the log to show both the set point and the range actually recorded; don't replace them with a single number or round them into a claim that the kettle held exactly 80 C.

june 16, batch D-215, is 24 kg cotton totes in indigo vat V3, also handled by Mara. start 07:20. the vat was at 22 C. there were three dips of four minutes, with 10 minutes airing between dips. pH was 10.7 at the start and 10.5 at 08:10. rinse happened at 08:44. the note compares the resulting shade as lighter than D-214, so say it as a comparison with that earlier batch, not as a general shade standard. two tote panels were set apart for a second look. there is no instruction yet to re-dye them, so show the hold note without deciding what happens next. the panels are part of this batch, not a new batch code.

there is also a spoken note from Mara about D-215, quote her exact words in the log: “the shade looks warmer under the loading-bay lamps”. keep it as an observation in quotation marks. daylight swatches were checked at 09:20, but there was no final approval recorded. don't turn Mara's comment or the daylight check into approval, rejection, or a color correction instruction. i want that distinction visible if you use a note field or a short observation subsection. the quote is about the lighting where the shade was viewed, not a new measurement and not a change to the recorded comparison with D-214.

please include a compact numbered section for the three batch records, in date order, and give each record its batch code, date, fiber and weight, dye or colorant, equipment, operator, process readings and times, rinse, and shade or status note where provided. after those entries a short equipment section would help keep the cleanup details from getting lost in the batch data. vat V3 was drained after D-215, and its rinse water was clear by 09:15. kettle K2 was rinsed at 10:30. hoses H-4 and H-6 were tagged, with H-4 assigned to the vat and H-6 to the kettle. don't imply that the two hoses were swapped or that a cleaning test beyond the clear-water note was done.

one separate materials note is for the madder extract used on M-089: the lot was stored on the upper dry shelf before use. the alum was weighed for that batch at 0.96 kg, which matches the stated 8 percent of 12 kg fiber. keep the storage detail with the material note rather than suggesting a new handling rule. for D-214, the natural indigo container was returned to the blue cabinet after the run. those are the only storage notes i have; the log should not assign storage locations to the remaining materials or say stock was replenished.

finish with the distinct end-of-day information, not a repeated summary of the three shades: the floor log was closed at 11:05 on june 16, and the next scheduled use of V3 is not listed in these notes. don't infer a next job or recommend one. use clear headings and concise wording, keep the june 14 through june 16 scope, and leave missing details unstated rather than filling them in. make it a prompt for preparing the log from this material, not the completed log itself.", "output": "Create a textile dye log for the three workshop days, June 14–16, at Bellmere Textile Works. Cover only the batches and equipment notes below; do not turn this into a general dyeing guide or a yearly report. Use the supplied figures and keep operator names and batch codes with the correct work. Make the log easy to scan for someone reviewing what happened on the floor. Send the finished log to Ellis, not Leonie.

Use a title that includes the date span. Arrange the batch records in date order in a compact numbered section. For each record, include the batch code, date, fiber and weight, dye or colorant, equipment, operator, process readings and times, rinse, and any supplied shade or status note. Keep measured values distinct from targets or set points, and distinguish observations from approvals. Do not add missing details or infer outcomes.

1. **June 14 — D-214:** Cotton twill, 38 kg; natural indigo in vat V3; operator Mara. Start time: 06:40. Vat target: 22 C; recorded reading: 21.5 C. Prewet for 15 minutes, then three dips of four minutes each, with 12 minutes of airing between dips. Rinse at 08:12. The after-drying swatch looked deep blue. Do not describe an indigo recipe or imply that this swatch represents every piece of cloth in the workshop.

2. **June 15 — M-089:** Wool scarves, 12 kg; madder extract in kettle K2; operator Jo. Start time: 09:05. Alum mordant: 8 percent of fiber weight. Kettle set point: 80 C; recorded readings during the run: 78–81 C. Hold for 45 minutes; rinse at 10:02. Shade note: muted rust. Keep this record separate from the cotton and indigo batches. Preserve the difference between the set point and the recorded range; do not replace them with one number or claim the kettle held exactly 80 C.

3. **June 16 — D-215:** Cotton totes, 24 kg; indigo in vat V3; operator Mara. Start at 07:20; vat at 22 C. Three dips of four minutes each, with 10 minutes of airing between dips. pH: 10.7 at the start and 10.5 at 08:10. Rinse at 08:44. The recorded shade comparison is lighter than D-214. Two tote panels were set apart for a second look; record that status without deciding whether they will be re-dyed. They remain part of D-215, not a separate batch.

Include Mara’s spoken note about D-215 exactly as an observation in quotation marks: “the shade looks warmer under the loading-bay lamps”. Daylight swatches were checked at 09:20, but no final approval was recorded. Do not turn the quote or the daylight check into an approval, rejection, color-correction instruction, new measurement, or change to the comparison with D-214.

After the numbered batch records, include a short equipment section. Vat V3 was drained after D-215, and its rinse water was clear by 09:15. Kettle K2 was rinsed at 10:30. Hoses H-4 and H-6 were tagged: H-4 was assigned to the vat and H-6 to the kettle. Do not imply that the hoses were swapped or that a cleaning test beyond the clear-water note was performed.

Add a separate materials note. The madder extract used on M-089 was stored on the upper dry shelf before use. Alum for that batch was weighed at 0.96 kg, matching the stated 8 percent of 12 kg of fiber. The natural indigo container for D-214 was returned to the blue cabinet after the run. These are the only storage notes provided; do not assign locations to other materials or say that stock was replenished.

End with the distinct closing information: the floor log was closed at 11:05 on June 16, and the next scheduled use of V3 is not listed in these notes. Do not infer a next job or recommend one. Keep the log within June 14–16 and leave all other missing details unstated."}]
